relevance.rationale: Proves that the embedding of Frechet smooth manifolds into the Cahiers topos of formal smooth sets preserves the projective limits defining infinite jet bundles, closing a previously tacit assumption in the comonadic formulation of PDE theory (diffieties inside jet bundles). The shared vocabulary with this corpus is a false friend and that is the useful finding. The corpus's jets -- prop:vertex-algebra-jet-relations, the recursive brane tower, the jet filtration and jet-order valuation -- are ALGEBRAIC: J^n(A) = A_n is a finite level of a vertex-algebra/arc-type tower whose prolongation L_{-1} promotes H^(n)(q) to H^(n+1)(q). No smooth manifold, no PDE, no infinite jet limit, no topos. A corpus grep for 'synthetic differential', 'Cahiers topos', 'diffiety' and 'comonad' returns zero hits across content/ and docs/audits/. Since the corpus never takes the projective limit this document's theorem is about, and never works in a smooth-geometry category, there is no statement here it can consume. Scope note (a): this document, as read, supplies nothing usable here. That is not a claim that synthetic differential geometry is irrelevant to the framework -- only that this particular technical lemma has no consumer, and a citation would be decorative.

proposedActions.rationale: Read the statement and the corpus's jet blocks side by side; the two notions of jet are different constructions in different categories, and no corpus block asserts anything this lemma would source.
